summary: Recorded the mechanism the two compaction children share, so a reader of the parent account can see in one entry why both paths inherit the drift: each derives the index it may compact from a value the node computes for itself — trim from the minimum of the accepted indexes the leader has recorded for the configuration (and it refuses an explicit index above that minimum), the snapshot call from the decided index of the node that receives the call — and neither bound is compared against the entries the node's own log contains. The fact cites the derivations as sources and the two receipts that exercised it: trim compacted index 7 and the snapshot call compacted index 8, both over logs of six indices of content, after the drift the parent question witnesses (ec3329dc273e452aa92bcd44652c116a events 9-15 and e70b8baa087246c78ea3a64f24b8e97c events 0-5). This complements the two stale-condition corrections from the previous turns, so both compaction behaviours now show their executed basis, and it gives the final report a single citable statement of the shared cause rather than two separate ones. No execution was requested this turn; incomplete are the parent drift's bound/repair probe after many more rounds and leader changes, the trim child's storage-side route probe, the snapshot child's peer and follower sampling, timers and loss triggers, larger clusters, persistence, and any further independent lead.
